newsitem.title: USA: Ahmanson modifies proxy to Great Western holders.
newsitem.headline: Ahmanson modifies proxy to Great Western holders.

text.p: HF Ahmanson & Co has sent Great Western Financial Corp shareholders a revised consent solicitation on Ahmanson's $6.6 billion merger offer, papers filed with federal regulators said.

In an letter accompanying the Securities Exchange Commission filing, Ahmanson chairman Charles Rinehart asked shareholders to return the consent cards by March 27 and to support proposals to "obtain the best price and treat all bidders equally, (and)...to negotiate with Ahmanson."
The revised consent solicitation now asks that Ahmanson and any other bona-fide bidder be given the same non-public information provided to rival bidder Washington Mutual Inc .
On March 6, three days after Ahmanson's original solicitation was mailed, the board of Great Western accepted a $6.25 billion "white knight" merger proposal by Washington Mutual.

The second revision waters down a proposal capping breakup fees at $100 million from a binding by-law amendment to a non-binding resolution. An Ahmanson spokesman said the change "reflects the reality" of Western Financial's agreement to a $195 million breakup fee if the Washington Mutual merger falls through.

Unchanged in the consent solicitation are proposals to "facilitate the eventual consummation of the Ahmanson merger proposal." They include a by-law amendment to require that Great Western's 1997 annual meeting be held by May 6, the Securities Exchange Commission filing says.

On February 18, Ahmanson sued Great Western in Delaware Chancery Court seeking to block Great Western from resorting to any defensive measures, such as a poison pill, to thwart an unsolicited takeover offer.
In a countersuit, Great Western challenged the validity of the breakup fee proposal in the consent solicitation. Attorney Rodman Ward told Reuters "I thought it was illegal and we moved to enjoin."
But the Ahmanson spokesman said "We will be amending our (lawsuit) to challenge the breakup fee."
The proposed merger with Washington Mutual must be approved by shareholders of Great Western, which has postponed indefinitely the annual meeting normally held on the fourth Tuesday in April.
A court spokeswoman said no hearing date has been scheduled in the competing lawsuits.
